after: ## Where this fits in the subject
alt: Four rows: A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating and D thinking critically, each with a one-line summary of top-band evidence. The same criteria apply across every discipline in the course.
caption: Four broad criteria, written to work for every discipline in the subject.

alt: Three facts, climate, terrain and resources, feed into a conceptual framework such as supply and demand or geographic accessibility, which produces a reasoned explanation of why a trade route developed. A weaker answer only states the facts; a stronger one connects them through the framework.
caption: Facts alone are recall; a conceptual framework turns them into an explanation that transfers.

alt: A weaker investigation uses one or two easily found sources without comment. A stronger one starts from a clear research question, consults a government report, a news article and a firsthand community account, evaluates each for reliability and relevance, and only then draws conclusions.
caption: A range of source types, each evaluated against the question, before any conclusion.

alt: Two responses on the same historical event. One is a chronological list of facts with no structure or referencing. The other builds a clear argument, attaches named, referenced sources to each point and uses period-appropriate terminology.
caption: Accurate facts are not enough: C rewards structure, referencing and precise terminology.

alt: Two historical accounts of the same event feed into an evaluation of the strengths and weaknesses of each, which leads to a substantiated conclusion about which interpretation the evidence best supports. A weaker answer presents one interpretation as simply correct.
caption: Top-band D weighs more than one interpretation before reaching a supported judgement.

after: ## Connecting the four criteria to a single coursework unit
alt: A single local-issue investigation runs A, framing the issue with conceptual knowledge, then B, researching it, then C, a structured referenced write-up, then D, a critical evaluation. A dashed arrow shows that strong D evaluation depends on B research having gathered more than one perspective.
caption: The criteria build on each other inside one piece of coursework.
